answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-memory-hard compute-proof-work per identity to act as a secure kernel for the network. The verifier enforces this by checking if every hash output matches a unique, ephemeral task, treating each identity like a delicate whisper that must be earned by raw energy expenditure. While an honest agent pays this cost once, an attacker trying to flood the lagoon of the ledger with 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, hitting a wall of processing exhaustion. Fraud triggers a permanent identity burn, though the mechanism assumes no pooled hashing.
